# scriptt

> scriptt (written script<T>) is two Claude Code hooks and a file of Python types, `.scriptt/world.py`. Before Claude reads each message of the user, a small local decision model, d1, turns each request in it into a typed call from `world.py` and gives every word a type. When Claude stops, the Stop hook checks each call against the files written and the commands run in the transcript, and sends Claude back at most twice. Version 0.1.7.

Facts for an agent that sets scriptt up in a project:

- It needs Python 3.14 or later. It uses the standard library only.
- Install, in the folder of the project: `curl -fsSL https://scriptt.ai/install.sh | sh`. It writes `.scriptt/harness.py`, `.scriptt/agree.py`, `.scriptt/scriptt16.py`, `.scriptt/SKILL.md` and `.scriptt/world.py`, then runs `python3.14 .scriptt/harness.py install`. That adds a UserPromptSubmit hook and a Stop hook to `.claude/settings.local.json`, copies the skill to `.claude/skills/scriptt/SKILL.md`, and writes `.scriptt/config.json` if there is none. An existing `.scriptt/world.py` is not replaced.
- The public release of d1 is pending. The user must name an endpoint that they already have. `.scriptt/config.json` has 1 of 2 shapes:
  - A System One endpoint: `{"url": "http://127.0.0.1:8791/v1/systemone", "body": {"model": "d1-2B-MLX-8bit"}}`
  - A CoreAI endpoint: `{"url": "http://HOST:PORT/v1/decide", "key_file": "PATH TO THE FILE WITH THE TOKEN", "body": {"model": "d1-2b", "priority": "bulk", "autoload": true}}`
- With no d1, each hook prints 1 line on stderr that starts with `scriptt:`, and Claude Code goes on.
- `.scriptt/world.py` declares the project's vocabulary as Python types: an enum for each closed list of named things, a dataclass for each thing made of named fields, `NewType` brands (`Asked` for the user's words, `Written` for an agent's), `Many[T]`, `Maybe[T]` and `Later[T]`, and functions. A function is something a message can ask for. Its 1-line docstring completes the sentence "The text asks the reader to ...". The installed `world.py` is an example from another project. Propose a `world.py` for the project (5 to 10 functions) and write it only after the user says yes.
- Test, with no Claude Code session: `echo '{"hook_event_name": "UserPromptSubmit", "session_id": "setup-test", "prompt": "THE MESSAGE"}' | python3.14 .scriptt/harness.py`. It prints JSON. `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext` is the block that the agent receives, and it starts with `scriptt:`. Each reading is saved as 1 line of `.scriptt/events.jsonl` (form 5).
- `python3.14 .scriptt/harness.py serve` opens the board on `http://127.0.0.1:8787`: each message with every word linked to its type. The user drags types onto words and values into arguments. Each change goes through the engine, and an accepted change is kept on every rerun.
- The Claude desktop app can draw the reading on each message. In a terminal session of Claude Code: `/plugin install scriptt --marketplace maxtheman/scriptt`.
- Remove: delete the 2 `harness.py` entries from `.claude/settings.local.json`, then `.claude/skills/scriptt/` and `.scriptt/`.

## Files

- [install.sh](https://scriptt.ai/install.sh): the installer
- [SKILL.md](https://scriptt.ai/SKILL.md): what the agent does when a prompt arrives with a block that starts "scriptt:"
- [world.py](https://scriptt.ai/world.py): the starter world, with the rules for types in its docstring
- [harness.py](https://scriptt.ai/harness.py): the 2 hooks, the installer and the local server
- [agree.py](https://scriptt.ai/agree.py) and [scriptt16.py](https://scriptt.ai/scriptt16.py): the engine
- [The board](https://scriptt.ai/board/?demo): the board on the text of the home page, with the engine running in the browser
- [Roadmap](https://scriptt.ai/roadmap.md)
